voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: The sea south of Africa, nineteen seventy-nine. An American satellite saw a double flash, the signature of a nuclear test.
That day, President Carter wrote in his diary: either South Africa, Israel using a ship at sea, or nothing.
Air Force planes flew twenty-five sorties there, sampling the air. They found no fallout.
Five months later, he wrote of a growing belief among his scientists that Israel had conducted a test.
Publicly, a White House panel called it probably not nuclear. The diary stayed private until twenty-ten. No government has confirmed a test.
